provenance.method: Complete edited reading adaptation of the supplied bilingual working text: twenty source units grouped into 15 short reading chunks. Two editorial changes: the unresolved action behind the door is replaced with a neutral statement of the supported location; the redundant wording “Tonina daħlet ġewwa hi wkoll” is shortened to “Tonina daħlet hi wkoll”. Other source wording and all translations are retained. This is an editorial reading adaptation, not a verbatim transcript or an official answer key. The ten bilingual comprehension prompts remain unscored.

items.maltese: Kienet dejjem moħħha fil-ġirien. U trid tkun taf x'inhu jagħmel dak u x'inhi tagħmel l-oħra.
items.english: She was always preoccupied with the neighbours. And she wants to know what that man is doing and what the other woman is doing.

items.maltese: Kienet tqatta' ħin twil jew fil-bieb tad-dar jew fit-tieqa, ħalli tara x'inhu jiġri madwarha.
items.english: She used to spend a long time either in the doorway or at the window, so that she could see what was happening around her.

items.maltese: Darba waħda, waqt li kienet qed issajjar, semgħet ħafna għajjat barra fit-triq.
items.english: One day, while she was cooking, she heard a lot of shouting outside in the street.

items.maltese: Tonina mill-ewwel intebħet li kienet ġrat xi ħaġa, u wiċċha xegħel bil-ferħ.
items.english: Tonina immediately realised that something had happened, and her face lit up with joy.

items.maltese: Marret tara x'kien qiegħed jiġri, u hemm sabet li xi ġirien kienu qed jiġġieldu u jitgħajru.
items.english: She went to see what was happening and found that some neighbours were quarrelling and calling each other names.

items.maltese: Tonina kienet wara l-bieb tad-dar tagħha, minn fejn setgħet tara kulma kien qiegħed jiġri fit-triq.
items.english: Tonina was behind the door of her house, from where she could see everything that was happening in the street.

items.maltese: Hija baqgħet hemm barra, għax ma riedet titlef xejn minn dak li kien għaddej fit-triq.
items.english: She stayed outside because she did not want to miss anything that was happening in the street.

items.maltese: Min-naħa l-oħra, kellha xi ftit biża' li jekk jiġu l-pulizija jistgħu jtellgħuha bħala xhud.
items.english: On the other hand, she was somewhat afraid that, if the police came, they might call her as a witness.

items.maltese: Tant kienet mitlufa tara dik it-tilwima li nsiet li kellha l-ikel fuq in-nar.
items.english: She was so absorbed in watching that dispute that she forgot she had food on the stove.

items.maltese: Meta spiċċat il-ġlieda u l-ġirien li kienu qed jitgħajru daħlu ġewwa f'darhom, Tonina daħlet hi wkoll biex tkompli ssajjar u tlesti l-ikel.
items.english: When the quarrel ended and the neighbours who had been calling each other names went back into their house, Tonina also went inside to continue cooking and finish the food.

items.maltese: Imma kif qorbot lejn il-kċina, Tonina xammet riħa ta' ikel maħruq. “Ara xi ġrali! Ara xi ġrali!” Bdiet tibki u tgħajjat Tonina.
items.english: But as she approached the kitchen, Tonina smelled burnt food. “Look what has happened to me! Look what has happened to me!” Tonina began crying and shouting.

items.maltese: Ftit ħin wara wasal ir-raġel tagħha mix-xogħol, u ma kellhiex ikel x'tagħtih.
items.english: A little later her husband arrived home from work, and she had no food to give him.

items.maltese: U għal dakinhar Tonina u r-raġel kellhom jieklu biċċtejn ħobż bil-ġobon, għax l-ikel kien inħaraq kollu.
items.english: So that day Tonina and her husband had to eat two pieces of bread with cheese because all the food had burnt.

items.maltese: “M'hemmx li titgħallem int,” qalilha żewġha. “Lill-ġirien ħallihom.” Imma Tonina baqgħet dejjem moħħha fil-ġirien.
items.english: “You never learn,” her husband told her. “Leave the neighbours alone.” But Tonina remained preoccupied with the neighbours.

items.maltese: Kif jgħidu, min jitwieled tond ma jmutx kwadru.
items.english: As they say, someone born round does not die square: ingrained habits do not easily change.

items.maltese: 1. Fuq min kienet taħseb Tonina l-ħin kollu?
items.english: Who was Tonina thinking about all the time?

items.maltese: 2. X'semgħet Tonina barra fit-triq?
items.english: What did Tonina hear outside in the street?

items.maltese: 3. Minn fejn kienet tara x'kien qed jiġri?
items.english: From where could she see what was happening?

items.maltese: 4. Għaliex kienet tibża' mill-pulizija?
items.english: Why was she afraid of the police?

items.maltese: 5. X'nsiet Tonina fuq in-nar?
items.english: What did Tonina forget on the stove?

items.maltese: 6. X'riħa xammet ħdejn il-kċina?
items.english: What smell did she notice near the kitchen?

items.maltese: 7. Għaliex ma kellhiex ikel x'tagħti lir-raġel tagħha?
items.english: Why did she have no food to give her husband?

items.maltese: 8. X'kielu Tonina u r-raġel tagħha dakinhar?
items.english: What did Tonina and her husband eat that day?

items.maltese: 9. X'qalilha tagħmel żewġha dwar il-ġirien?
items.english: What did her husband tell her to do about the neighbours?

items.maltese: 10. Tonina bidlet id-drawwa tagħha fl-aħħar?
items.english: Did Tonina change her habit in the end?
